n: The Lord addresses all twelve tribes — the whole family He rescued from Egypt. The message is for northern Israel and southern Judah alike.
Being chosen carries responsibility. God “knew” Israel in a close covenant relationship, so He holds them more accountable, not less.
A series of questions shows cause and effect. Two people walking together have agreed to meet; likewise, a prophet speaks because God has met with him.

f.w: Can two walk together, except they be agreed?

n: A lion roars only when it has caught prey. Amos implies that when God “roars” through a prophet, judgment is real.

f.g: A strong young lion, hunting on its own.

n: A bird is not caught without a trap, and a trap doesn’t spring for nothing. Every effect has a cause — including Israel’s coming troubles.
A trumpet in the city makes people afraid. When disaster comes, the Lord is behind it. Amos teaches that God governs history.
A key verse for Latter-day Saints: God does nothing without first revealing His plans to His prophets. He warns before He acts.

f.w: he revealeth his secret unto his servants the prophets

f.g: Hebrew sod — the private counsel of God.

n: Just as everyone fears when a lion roars, a prophet cannot keep quiet when God speaks. Amos explains why he must preach.
Ironically, Philistines and Egyptians are invited to look at Samaria’s chaos and oppression. Even pagans would be shocked.

f.g: Capital of the northern kingdom of Israel.

n: Israel’s rich no longer know how to do right; their mansions are full of goods taken by violence.

f.g: Their treasure houses are stocked with stolen wealth.

n: An enemy will surround the land and plunder the palaces. Assyria conquered Samaria in 722 BC.
A shepherd might rescue only scraps — two legs or an ear — to prove a sheep was killed by a lion. So only scraps of Israel’s luxury-loving elite will survive.

f.w: two legs, or a piece of an ear

f.g: The Hebrew is unclear; possibly “on the damask cushion of a couch.”

n: The Lord calls witnesses to testify against Israel (“the house of Jacob”).

f.g: God of armies — Lord over all heavenly and earthly powers.

n: Judgment will strike Bethel, where Jeroboam I set up a golden calf. The horns on the altar corners, a place of refuge, will be broken off.
The wealthy’s winter and summer homes and their ivory-paneled mansions will be destroyed. Archaeologists have found carved ivory pieces in Samaria.
